step1_analysis.description: A CMOS Schmitt trigger circuit with variable-threshold feedback. It uses feedback transistors (XM5, XM6) driven by the inverted output to alter the switching thresholds, creating hysteresis. This block is typically used in relaxation oscillators or signal conditioning for temperature sensors.

paper_reference.title: A BJT-Based CMOS Temperature Sensor with a 3.6pJ·K2-Resolution FoM

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the pull-down network (XM2, XM3) overcoming the pull-up network (XM4, XM6). With equal sizing, NMOS is stronger, so the threshold is slightly below VDD/2.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard Schmitt trigger behavior in 1.8V CMOS.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the pull-up network (XM4, XM8) overcoming the pull-down network (XM2, XM3, XM5).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Must be lower than vth_plus to provide hysteresis.
Typical hysteresis for a 1.8V Schmitt trigger is 200-400mV.

sky130_expected.calculation: Time from input crossing threshold to output crossing threshold.
Integral of VDD * I(VDD) during a switching event.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 3.6pJ for the entire sensor. A single Schmitt trigger will consume much less, typically in the fJ range.

step3_testbench.description: Measures Schmitt trigger thresholds, hysteresis, propagation delay, and energy per operation using a slow triangular wave followed by fast pulses.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Schmitt Trigger Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N2 N5 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N5 N0 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N3 N0 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N5 N0 N4 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N3 N2 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N4 N2 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N2 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N4 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

* Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VN1 N1 0 0
* PWL: Slow ramp up/down for hysteresis, then fast pulses for delay/energy
VIN N0 0 PWL(0 0 40u 1.8 80u 0 81u 0 81.01u 1.8 85u 1.8 85.01u 0 90u 0)

.control
tran 100p 90u

* Measure Thresholds and Hysteresis (from slow ramp)
meas tran vth_plus find v(N0) when v(N2)=0.9 rise=1
meas tran vth_minus find v(N0) when v(N2)=0.9 fall=1
let hysteresis = vth_plus - vth_minus
print hysteresis

* Measure Propagation Delay (from fast pulse)
meas tran t_pd_rise trig v(N0) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(N2) val=0.9 rise=2
meas tran t_pd_fall trig v(N0) val=0.9 fall=2 targ v(N2) val=0.9 fall=2
let t_pd = (t_pd_rise + t_pd_fall) / 2
print t_pd

* Measure Energy per Operation (during fast pulse window)
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
meas tran energy_pulse integ power from=81u to=86u
let energy_per_op = energy_pulse / 2
print energy_per_op

quit
.endc
